text_fidelity_a:
Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules This is the best deck building game EVER!!
I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.
text_fidelity_b: Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills This is not up to the typical quality of Melissa and Doug products in my opinion. There are 12 mini-projects in this "book"(it's an scruffy bubble envelope with other envelopes inside), and each has some very basic scissor projects. The first one, for instance, has your child cutting in straight lines to create a simple memory game. The second one builds on this, adding some cross-cutting, and so forth.

Each kit is good enough, and the variety is greatly appreciated by the kiddos. In some instances, the instructions needed a little work, while in others, they were perfect. In each case, they're language independent and entirely taught through pictures, which is great for helping the kiddos follow along and do the projects somewhat independently.

There are two pairs of scissors included in this package - a straight pair, and a "scrapbooking" scissor that cuts "teeth" - but these safety scissors are entirely too "safety" for me. The straight one works well enough at first, while the teeth scissors barely worked at all. Their entirely plastic frame wears out with minimal use. There are no metal parts on them, outside of the screws. We had trouble making clean cuts as we approached the middle of the kits, and by the end, we just switched to metal scissors as we were mangling the paper more than doing actual cutting.

The problem with the scissors, as well as the complete lack of a storage solution for these projects as they're in progress is enough for me to rate this kit lower than I normally do. My kit arrived mispacked, so I received two #4 projects, and no #3 project. Good projects can be had here, but bring some of your own materials.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills

text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Backyard Barbeque Get Out 'N Grill Little Tykes = Shoddy

1) you cannot push the red 'igniter' button without pushing over the whole grill, it's so stiff. My toddle certainly can't do it at all.

2) the pieces don't fit together properly, as usual with Little Tykes toys. Ugh. The side panels (the sink and burner pieces) don't mate properly, so the result is very slanted and everything slowly slides off.

3) incredibly light weight. Topples very easily.

4) the doors won't open or shut completely without an adult assisting. My two year old is very particular, and get frustrated that he can't close the doors all the way.

5) the two grilling areas are very small. The slippery food provided falls off incredibly easily. That is not conducive to toddlers enjoying themselves. I would rather have a large flat grilling area that kiddies could enjoy instead of two poorly placed small ones.

6) the faucet handle doesn't move. It really looks like it could. How much more difficult could it be to make that happen? Apparently- for a company that gets everything else wrong- it's far tough.

TL,DR: if you like spending money on cheap products, get it.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Backyard Barbeque Get Out 'N Grill

text_fidelity_a:
Little Live Scruff-A-Luvs Cutie Cuts: Shave, Reveal and Style, Plush Rescue Pet - Pink Puppy I see a lot of reviews complaining, but I got this for my 6 year old's birthday and she loves it. No, the fur doesn't really "shave off" it's more like you comb it off and grab it. It takes parental involvement and it's messy, but it's meant to be an experience, which it fully delivers. My daughter did the unboxing and loved finding all the surprises. We "shaved" her pup and gave it a bath in a bowl at my kitchen table. We set up a "drying station" with my hair dryer and a towel. The entire experience was magical and bonding for my daughter and I. We giggled and guessed if we would get the Frenchie or Yorkie and wondered what color it's nails would turn. The bath was fun and a bit messy, and blow drying took a while (mostly mom, she got bored) but her favorite part was grooming the Frenchie (it was easy to tell) and adding the little accessories. The surprise factor was 100% on point. The whole time the suspense was palpable for her. She was guessing the whole time and we came up with names for it.
Don't buy this toy if you can't be bothered to spend an hour playing with your child.
Don't buy this toy expecting a 5-7 year old to do this independently.
This toy is clearly meant for interactive play with an adult.
This toy was a wonderful addition to our homeschooling dramatic play for kindergarten.

If you want a toy that allows you and your child to pretend to own a grooming salon, this toy is perfect. Have everything prepared ahead of time. We put a table cloth down and a bowl of warm water with shampoo, then in a separate area we had the drying and grooming station. Expect to spend at least 45-60 minutes on this adorable experience. It's wonderful for people who enjoy playing with their kids. Our whole family loves it.
text_fidelity_b: Little Live Scruff-A-Luvs Cutie Cuts: Shave, Reveal and Style, Plush Rescue Pet - Pink Puppy

text_fidelity_a:
LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink My grandmother purchased these as a special gift for 2 girls ages just turned 2 and almost 4 as there was some resentment from their new baby brother. She told me there were many good reviews and thought it could help the girls stay busy when Mommy needs to help their brother. These are a life saver. We even got the headphones to match so there is not fights over I can't hear my book because of your book. It was also amazing we got 2 system to solve fights. I just took a label maker and put each of their names on them.

They did get the first series of books. However the almost 4 year old is flying through the books as they are easy for her. So we just got one next level up book and that seems to be more her speed. Each system we were able to download 10 books and the sample book. Unfortunately it won't fit more. So as the older one gets more advanced, we will delete the younger books.

The system does take AA batteries, so I suggest keeping a spare set on hand. The downside is there is no warning of low battery, so it helps to have new ones ready to go. You also need a small screw driver to put them in.

I also suggest getting (or making as I did) a tote bag for them to store their system and books in.

The device is easy to open. They do need assistance with the books sometimes. I do wish the stylus pen cord was a bit longer, but that may be a safety thing too so the kids don't get hurt.

Even if you cannot afford the books right away (keep an eye as I often see them go on sale for $5-6 here) the starter book has 5 pages of activities to entertain the children.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink

Hasbro Gaming Scrabble Crossword Game What you have here is one fine game. Classic, traditional, great for all ages.

Know a bunch of words? Short ones? Long ones? Skinny ones? Know any big fat words you just can't use anywhere else? Use them here. Show off how big your vocabulary is, and that you know how to use it. Of course, there are rules about which ones count, but mostly, regular words are OK. Just nothing with capitals or foreign words, unless of course, you are from somewhere else, but then, they aren't foreign any longer, are they?

Order up a serving of Scrabble. Figure out if you need this version or the deluxe version (which is mighty cool.) If you are new to Scrabble, this is the version to start with.

When you get the game in the mail, call up some friends, turn on some tunes, crack open something tasty and cold, and start munching a few chips. This ain't a game you gotta be smart to play. I've seen guys who only know small words, but they could see the best ways to use them. Vocabs don't win the game. Thinking on your feet will win the game.

I fully recommend Scrabble.

Anthony Trendl

text_fidelity_a:
Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.
The artwork is very nice, with a clean, simple aesthetic. Very Japanese!
I have two very nit picky complaints about it. One of the categories on the board pieces is pines. They look very much like cacti to me. The other is that on the black pieces the black hair of the characters kind of disappears. I wish they had outlined them somehow.
All in all a great game. Highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

SmartLab Toys Squishy Human Body with 21 Removable Body Parts with Anatomy Book This product has the potential to be an incredible teaching tool which is why I initially purchased it. However, it is evident after ordering this item (even after a replacement of the original product that was initially delivered--replacement is shown in pictures above), that there are reoccurring issues with this item that are extremely problematic.

You can see how there are pieces of this product that come lodged incorrectly including the skull which does not stay in its designated hole. The large intestine looks like it's already been pulled apart by a child passed its point of stretch as it is extremely thin at the connection area.

Also--I if I as a teacher could not even put this item in full back together, I can only imagine how difficult this would be for a child of any age to maneuver as well.

If this company would just give more effort into putting out a quality product it would be extremely useful across-the-board and save them so much money in returns if they would just take the small effort to fix these ongoing issues that so many purchasers report.

I was able to get a 25% refund on my initial purchase with being able to keep the item as I explained I do not want to do a third replacement bit instead that I would rather just find a innovative way to make the issues I've experienced usable for teaching my students.

If you get this product don't settle for a poor quality item...they used to be made so well and now this company has made cheaply made pieces of it the regular. Stick to your guns on insisting on either a working product and/or a refund.

Wish you all the best with this item.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys Squishy Human Body with 21 Removable Body Parts with Anatomy Book

text_fidelity_a:
Estes Syncro X Nano R/C Quadcopter, White (Discontinued by manufacturer) Great quadcopter which is hampered by a so-so controller. I applaud Hubsan (Estes is their distributor in the US and uses the Estes brand on these Hubsan Q4 nanos) for making a controller with the same size as the quad. The boards in these nano-controllers are exactly the same as in the Hubsan X4 controller, with a few functions disabled. The function I really want (and I'm not sure exactly why they disabled this) is the 'Expert' level. This basically gives the sticks 100% range (rather than about 30% on the basic level). You need this extra range on the nano because it tends to drift due to its light weight. [[ASIN:B00IZC6C8E Hubsan H107L X4 Mini RTF RC Quadcopter]] controllers pair with the Estes Synchro X Nano with no problem. Using the bigger controller allows you to do flips, which are actually easier indoors than with the Hubsan X4, because the light nanos don't drop as much during a flip. Overall a well engineered and implemented toy that is cheap and lots of fun.

Suggestions: purchase extra blades from RCSuperstore.com ($2.38 a set) and extra batteries (~$4 ea.) The batteries are taped to the board, but you can just pull them off and substitute light velcro, leave the top off and swap out batteries just like you do with your X4. The batteries need to be secured in place in the nano, or they would constantly cause drift. If you travel, take a phone charger to charge up the battery. In general, these batteries will wear quickly unless your charger has power management. Buy an [[ASIN:B00IBDOB5I Anker® 40W 5-Port Family-Sized Desktop USB Charger with PowerIQ™ Technology for iPhone 5s 5c 5; iPad Air mini; Galaxy S5 S4; Note 3 2; the new HTC One (M8); Nexus and More (White)]]and your batteries will charge much faster and last much longer.
text_fidelity_b: Estes Syncro X Nano R/C Quadcopter, White (Discontinued by manufacturer)

MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys The box says that this Magnet Building Sticks set is for ages six and up, but I'm really enjoying playing with it as an adult. I think younger kids would need some help to do the suggested building projects, but using the set to build things is easy. The set includes 120 magnetic sticks, 40 steel balls, and a gray bag with a drawstring to hold the set if you don't want to use the original packaging. The balls are 1 inch across, and the sticks are 2.25 inches long and 1/4 inch across.

The magnets hold together strong enough to basically stay where you put them but not so strong that it's difficult to pull things apart. The more stable builds (which have many triangles instead of squares) hold their shape well as you build them. Some of the building projects that have a more open structure have a tendency to collapse during certain stages of building, and then they start to attach to parts that they aren't supposed to. It can be a mess to straighten out. Once I realized that this could happen, I was more careful to stabilize these open structures as I built them, so this hasn't been a problem since.

The set also came with pictures of a number of projects. Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ The quality is great, and the concept is very creative. We play with this everyday, and think it’s fun, but there’s some thoughts I want to share:

-The clear bolts are somewhat difficult to find on the carpet. I wish the ends (tips) were colored to help make them stand out since they blend into the floor and surfaces.

-The drill bit is always falling out, and it’s also clear, so it can be hard to find it when it falls, and it’s cumbersome to have to keep putting it back in the drill repeatedly.

-The drill has two directions to tighten and loosen the bolts, which is adjusted with the sliding control. The drill itself works very well at tightening and loosening, but it gets a little involved helping my child make adjustments on the drill. My child wants to tighten and loosen a single bolt at a time before moving onto the next bolt, so we’re constantly flip-flopping the controls. Maybe slightly older preschoolers would be more independent using the drill, but I think a manual tool (like a screwdriver) would be the easiest to operate.

Our favorite part of this whole set is dropping all of the bolts in the back of the truck and then opening the hatch to watch all of them tumble out. My child thinks this is hilarious and is by far the best part!

In short, I think this whole set is a great concept, but is slightly overcomplicated. I really feel a simple screwdriver would help simplify the need to shift around buttons constantly, and would even help with dexterity and motor skills more than the cumbersome drill.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+

He is very active and loves music. “If You’re Happy and You Know It” is one of the songs he is very familiar with and enjoys. That being said, unfortunate he was not too enthralled with this monkey. I’ve played the song and the clapping game for him several times. He’ll observe it but does not interact with it.

The monkey is well made and soft, except for the arms and abdomen when squeezed. You can feel the hard “skeletal” support that is necessary to produce the movement in the monkey. The on/off switch is located on the bottom under a Velcro closure furry flap. I would not recommend that this monkey be used for snuggling by children. My thought is that it is most appealing to infants 4 months to about a year. Of course not all children are alike. The young voice in Clappy is very sweet and inviting. The arm movements are rhythmic and move to the beat of the song. His cheeks light up with a soft red light during the song. It is visually appealing. For the cost, there should be more music programmed into it. Over-all, the appeal depends on your child. As for my grandson.... not so much. In fairness, I do have to wonder if “Clappy” would have received a more enthusiastic welcome when he was younger.

text_fidelity_a: Petit Collage Animal Friends Magnetic Game Board with Mix & Match, Ideal for Ages 3+, Includes Mag Play Scene Treehouse Party, 74 Count This magnetic playset has 72 magnetic pieces, 2 backdrop scenes, and a box to hold the set. The set is made for ages three and up. The sturdy cardboard box has a lid that lifts up and can be set in a groove in the sides of the box so it acts like an easel. The bottom side of the lid has a magnetic backdrop of a tree house. There is a thin, magnetic backdrop in the box that you can place over this scene to transform it into a picnic scene. There are four characters: a rabbit, a bear, a fox, and a squirrel. There are various pieces for play imaginative play, from birds, bees, leaves, and flowers to furniture and food. The smaller pieces are about half an inch square, so they could be a choking hazard or easily lost if not kept attached to the backdrop or in the box. The pieces are thick enough (just over 1 cm) that they should endure play fairly well. They easy popped out of the magnetic sheets that they initially came in. The magnet strength is strong enough to hold them in place during play or travel while still easy to remove from the backdrop. Overall, if your child likes imaginative play, this can be a fun set. text_fidelity_a:
LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old LEGO have been hit by the inflation bug, and they've upped their prices recently on all sets. Nowhere is that more clear than in this set, which is very expensive for what you get.

Targeted towards the younger audience who is just beyond Duplo blocks, this is a pretty simple set with a pretty doofy-looking dragon that clearly skews younger, and doesn't fit in well with the rest of the Ninjago line, which is undoubtedly the LEGO line that has the highest "cool factor". So to judge this against a regular Ninjago set, this set woudl be a clear loser.

But it's really not for the older kids who can handle a ninja base or a 900-piece battle wagon, it's for littles. And for them, this is a fun set, but it is outrageously priced for what you get. It's essentially a few minifigs, a small dragon, a small set-piece, and a motorbike. Its simple to put together, but if you're working with a 4-year old, you probably need a little parental assistance.

For mini-munchkins, I suppose this would be a fun set to play with, but at close to $50 at the time of this writing, you are paying a very pretty penny for the fun you can have with it. At half that cost, and for the right audience, I'd find it a 4-star value. For what it is, I can't rank it higher than 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Mix BY HAND all ingredients, except flour and chips (mixing by hand makes them taste better, trust me).
Then add flour and chips and stir BY HAND. Bake @ 350 for 9-11 minutes on ungreased cookie sheet. Enjoy the preciouses.
Note: makes a buttload of cookies, so you might want to halve the recipe.

text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

Magic the Gathering Cards - Khans of Tarkir - Booster Packs (6 Pack Lot) I ordered 18 boosters (3 of 6 booster bundles) and two of the bundles showed signs of being tampered with. Extra cuts on the bottom edge of the pack, packs that were ridiculously easy to open -- I've never opened boosters that basically fall apart along one crimped edge consistently like these did. I really don't trust that someone hasn't sorted through these and skimmed the fetch lands out or something. I can't prove that they were tampered with, the right numbers of cards were all there in the right proportions, but it sure feel like this is some kind of scam the way those packs fell apart.

tl;dr: Stay away, get your boosters from sealed product like sealed booster boxes, sealed fat packs or sealed holiday boxes instead; the packs I got in bagged bundles from my seller were fishy as hell.

Greater Than Games Sentinels of The Multiverse Enhanced Card Game (2nd Edition) Sentinels of the multiverse is a cooperative card game where you and your friends play as super heroes from the sentinels comic universe fighting a villian in a few different locations. The game is pretty easy and straight forward, but not easy to win. We've had a lot of fun trying all the different combinations of locations, heroes and villians. There are plenty of expansions available to keep the game fresh, but even with just the heroes, villians and locations included in the game there is plenty to do.

Definitely pick up the "Enhanced" version over the previous version. It's usually only a few bucks more, but will get you a bigger box that can handle the expansions, card dividers for all included cards as well as dividers for all expansions and promo cards (available from sentinels website) as well as tokens to track damage, modifiers, etc. Previously this was done with a sheet of paper/pen.

Overall this is a fun cooperative card game. If you have any interest in card games and super heroes, this game is for you.
